chunks: And by this chain of narration, he said:

The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: Whoever delivers the message of a warrior (ghazi) is like one who has freed a slave, and he will be his partner in the reward of his military expedition.

key_terms.ثَوَابِ: thawab — divine spiritual reward earned through righteous deeds
key_terms.رَقَبَةً: raqabah — literally 'neck,' used idiomatically to mean a slave in classical Arabic jurisprudence
key_terms.غَازٍ: ghazi — a warrior who participates in military jihad in the path of God
key_terms.غَزْوَة: ghazwah — a military expedition or battle campaign

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on the reward for delivering a warrior's message?
ai.summary: This prophetic hadith establishes an important principle of spiritual merit: those who support warriors in jihad by carrying their messages earn equivalent reward to emancipating a slave — one of the highest meritorious acts in Islamic law. The Prophet draws a powerful analogy that democratizes spiritual reward: even those unable to fight personally can earn equal divine recompense through auxiliary service. For the early Muslim community engaged in military expeditions, this teaching was a profound motivation for all members of society to contribute to the collective effort according to their capacity.

en.hubeali: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The one who delivers a message of a combatant is like the one who freed a neck and he would be his participant in the Rewards of his battle’.
en.sarwar: 9. Through the same chain of narrators as that of the previous Hadith

the following is narrated: “One for conveying the message of a fighter for the cause of Allah, receives a reward equal to that for setting free a slave and will have a share in the reward for his fighting for the cause of Allah.”
